---
title: "ER2-ENGINE"
subtitle: "Run ER2 inside Quarto documents"
---

![](assets/logo.png){fig-alt="ER2-ENGINE: a Quarto engine for ER2" width="220" fig-align="center"}

[ER2](https://github.com/oeistools/ER2) is Python with mathematics built
in: `x^2` is a power, `1/3` is exact, `sym x` declares a symbol, and number
theory runs on PARI/GP. This extension makes it a Quarto language:
` ```{er2} ` cells execute, and they are highlighted as ER2.

```{er2}
sym x
f = (x + 1)^3
expand(f)
```

```{er2}
factor(2^64 + 1), phi(123456789), 1/3 + 1/6
```

Everything on this site — including the two cells above — was computed by
the engine as the page was built.

## Install

```bash
quarto add oeistools/ER2-ENGINE
```

You also need Quarto 1.9 or newer and ER2 itself; see
[Get started](getting-started.qmd).

## What you get

- **One ER2 session per document.** Symbols and values carry from cell to
  cell, and to inline code: $f =$ `{er2} latex(f)`.
- **Mathematics as mathematics.** A cell that ends in an expression shows
  it, as LaTeX when it has a LaTeX form.
- **Figures** from Matplotlib, numbered and cross-referenceable.
- **ER2 highlighting** — `sym`, `^^`, `5r` — with nothing to configure.
- **No Jupyter.** No kernel to install, no daemon to restart.

This is the sibling of
[PARI-GP-ENGINE](https://oeistools.github.io/PARI-GP-ENGINE/), built the
same way for a different language.
